### Architect · Answer

Event: `7d4c6b5a85b41c4165e30df542b320e4` · 2026-10-02T20:54:24Z

> Ruled. None of your three options; a fourth, which applies the owner's decision A in full.
> 
> (1) Agreed: no walk package. a is on time; b grows ~4 ms with H live and stays within R10. Walk work stays in K16.
> 
> (2) The rule is already the owner's (scheduling.md#responsiveness): each target counts the kernel a release build runs. K15 took the audits' time out of the windows. The split shows the audits still move the schedule: the scheduler charges audit time to the running budget and counts it against the slice. So the stand-in is requeued where a release kernel would run it on and take both notices in one slice. That is a gap in how the checked build keeps the rule, not a target question. So:
> - Not netting the requeue in the oracle: that is a guessed counterfactual schedule.
> - Not a per-width target and not excluding the seed: each widens or weakens, against the owner's rule.
> - Instead, K18 (Tier A, kernel, S; plan node added, needs K17): in a checked build an audit's time is charged to no budget and does not count against the running slice. The slice end and the charge start move forward by its length. Audits stay full, no target moves, the attacker is unchanged.
>   - Accepted on GATE1's two-lease fixture (e9ecc5ea5, seed 4) meeting the notice on both widths; no regression at seed 3 (sched-latency, kernel-containment); a recorded negative run (`audit-billed`) that misses.
>   - Brief: .wash/local/K18-implementer.md. Follow-up page docs/todo/audits-billed.md, and the residual on scheduling.md, on main at 307b5d818.
> 
> (3) GATE1: hold the WIP fold and change nothing. Please add K18 to GATE1's needs (GATE1 has started, so that is yours). GATE1 resumes unchanged on K18's merge: the sweep, the seed sentence, the bench, the fold and the re-review. INIT1 stays behind GATE1. K16 keeps needing GATE1, so there is no cycle.
